title: JBS Southern Hosts One-Of-A-Kind Backgrounding and Feeder Challenge

body_markdown:
In early September, 600 elite Angus steers were successfully inducted at Condah Hills in South West Victoria, marking the official start of the Optiweigh Yambinya Backgrounding and Feeder Challenge **.**


The first competition of its kind, the Challenge brings together cattle from vendors across southern Australia to generate objective performance data under identical conditions, measuring their journey across performance on grass, grain and eating quality **.**


With the support of the team at Condah Hills, the JBS Farm Assurance team successfully inducted all cattle into the competition and recorded their starting weights.


Over approximately 100 days of backgrounding, Optiweigh units located in each paddock will monitor the cattle’s weight gain, allowing growth and daily performance on grass to be tracked across each group.


Following the backgrounding phase, the cattle will move to JBS Yambinya Station, where they will be finished on a natural grain ration.


At the completion of the Challenge, the cattle will be processed and graded into JBS Farm Assurance’s premium Natural Grain-fed Portoro beef brand, providing insights across the entire journey from grass to grain and eating quality.


Lachie McKenzie of McKenzie Ag, which is generously hosting the backgrounding component at Condah Hills, said:


“When JBS approached us regarding the possibility of hosting the backgrounding component of the Yambinya Feeder Challenge, I was initially skeptical. It sounded like a huge amount of work and a major commitment from us in terms of taking up grazing capacity and time for our team. However, once I understood the magnitude of what was being proposed, the professionalism under which it was be conducted and the value to industry at large in the data that was going to be collected, we had to be involved. This is a ‘first of kind’ trial. Never before has a trial of this scale been undertaken that involves such detailed measurement across a backgrounding program, feedlot performance and carcass analytics. The benefit of this to cattle Breeders, Backgrounders, Feed-lotters and Processors is far-reaching. JBS should be commended for investing such a significant amount of time, money and effort to bring this Challenge to life. We are delighted to be involved and are excited to see the performance in the Cattle here at Condah Hills, and later at Yambinya Station and then at processing."
